prompt_text:
This figure summarizes how mouse embryonic stem cells balance self-renewal and differentiation through the FGF4–MEK–ERK pathway. At the top, cells from the blastocyst are shown maintaining pluripotency through Wnt/β-catenin, LIF, and inhibition of GSK3, while FGF4 activates ERK to drive commitment toward differentiation into embryonic or extraembryonic lineages. Blocking MEK together with GSK3 inhibition (“2i”) suppresses this differentiation-promoting pathway and helps preserve a naïve, self-renewing state.

The middle schematic expands the signaling network. ERK appears to phosphorylate several key pluripotency regulators, including KLF2, KLF4, and NANOG/associated factors, generally opposing the ground-state pluripotency program. LIF and BMP4 act through STAT3 and SMAD to support that ground state, whereas ERK signaling feeds into RSK and also affects protein stability and localization: KLF2 and KLF4 are shown being ubiquitinated and degraded, and KLF4 seems to shuttle between nucleus and cytoplasm. DUSP9 is included as a negative regulator of ERK.

The bottom table compares phenotypes under different genetic or culture conditions. Loss of Ras reduces proliferation, embryoid body formation, and teratoma formation; removing Erf rescues this. In 2i plus LIF these properties increase, whereas loss of Rsk lowers them, supporting ERK/RSK as important regulators of stem-cell behavior.
